dimensions.reasons: The submitted final-style render (.eval_workspace/exports/turbine_storyboard_cam01.png) clearly shows the requested overall scene: a three-bladed horizontal-axis turbine on an open field at dusk, with a low-angle composition, sunset sky, long cast shadow, and airborne debris/dust. Group A close views confirm a recognizable tower, nacelle, hub, and rotor.
issues: The drivetrain is not visibly represented as the requested complete gearbox/shaft/generator/brake assembly; the nacelle is largely an opaque simplified shell.
Airborne rectangular fragments read as synthetic confetti rather than falling leaves.
No submitted time sequence demonstrates actual rotor rotation or particle simulation behavior.

dimensions.reasons: The primary turbine structure is coherently assembled: the nacelle rests above the tower and the rotor is joined to the nacelle in Group A detail_nacelle_side.png and detail_drivetrain.png. The tower also reaches the ground and has a visible footing.
issues: The circular base appears as a thin disc laid on top of the grass rather than a credible embedded or substantial turbine foundation.

Numerous dust dots and especially brown rectangular fragments are visibly suspended throughout open air in cam_submitted.png and the author final render, with no readable source or natural falling behavior.
Particles pass through the turbine's immediate airspace and do not convincingly react to the tower or rotor.

dimensions.reasons: The tower, nacelle, hub, and three tapered blades have a strong, recognizable modern wind-turbine silhouette in all Group A wide and detail views. White painted turbine surfaces read clearly against the muted green-brown field and dusk sky.
issues: The nacelle is a very simplified rounded rectangular housing rather than a convincing engineered enclosure with discernible drivetrain-related detail.
Tower, nacelle, blades, and hub are nearly uniform white with limited material differentiation.
The airborne rectangles do not visually read as leaves.

dimensions.reasons: The author final image has a generally appealing sunset atmosphere, soft depth of field, plausible broad shadow, and a credible turbine silhouette. The background horizon and cloudy pink-gray sky provide a coherent outdoor context.
issues: The dense field of floating rectangular debris and dot-like spheres substantially reduces believability.
The grass is visibly a regular ribbed/grid-like ground texture rather than a natural open grassy field.
The final image is somewhat washed out at the horizon, while strong haze and depth of field obscure environmental detail.
Despite the requested spinning rotor and motion blur, the blades predominantly read as a static, sharply defined three-blade pose.

dimensions.reasons: Spatial organization is sound: the tall tapered tower is vertical on the field, the nacelle is mounted at its top, and a three-bladed rotor is placed in front of the nacelle. The 120-degree blade arrangement is clearly visible in Group A wide_front.png, wide_side.png, and wide_iso_high.png.
issues: The debris is distributed broadly around the turbine rather than visibly originating from or following a particularly believable wind path.
Yaw capability and internal shaft alignment cannot be confirmed visually through the opaque nacelle.

dimensions.reasons: The tower-to-rotor relationship reads as plausibly utility-scale: the long blades span a substantial fraction of the tower height, and the final camera framing establishes the turbine as very tall relative to the field and distant horizon.
issues: The tower appears quite thin and the nacelle relatively small/simple for the implied roughly 80 m hub-height machine.
The shallow, flat footing looks undersized and implausible for a turbine of this apparent scale.

dimensions.reasons: The dusk HDRI-like sky lighting and directional sun effect are effective in the author final render, producing a warm horizon, cool cloud cover, soft illumination on the white turbine, and a long ground shadow. The turbine surfaces read as clean painted matte material.
issues: The scene lacks the requested distinct material read across mechanical components because the internal components are not exposed and most visible turbine parts share the same white finish.
Bright horizon haze flattens contrast in portions of the final composition.
The grass material remains visibly patterned and artificial at wide-view scale.

dimensions.reasons: Visible essentials are present: a tapered tower, nacelle, hub, exactly three long blades, open field, dusk sky, sun-like directional shadowing, and particle-like airborne debris. Group A detail views also show small nacelle-top fittings and a rear inset.
issues: The requested gearbox, main shaft, high-speed shaft, generator, and brake are not visibly verifiable in the opaque nacelle.
No submitted animation frames establish that the rotor actually spins or that a Wind and Turbulence field drive the particles.
Dust and leaf effects are present in quantity but do not convincingly depict gravity-driven falling leaves and dust.
Motion blur is not clearly visible on the rotor in the submitted final render.

criteria.criterion: The coherent horizontal-axis turbine uses the specified tapered tubular tower and principal dimensions.
The nacelle is genuinely configured as yaw-capable on the tower.
The nacelle contains every named internal machine arranged as one plausible drivetrain.
The hub carries the complete dimensioned three-blade rotor.
The completed authored scene has believable relative scale and consistently estimated unspecified dimensions.
The final render uses readable and believable material distinctions without prescribing unique materials for fixed object or effect classes.
criteria.evidence: In the author final image turbine_storyboard_cam01.png, the turbine reads as smooth matte white with shaded seams, the field has a darker green-brown textured treatment, the sky is softly luminous and clouded, and the airborne brown fragments/darker dust specks separate visibly from both the turbine and background.

criteria.criterion: Enabled Wind and Turbulence fields participate in a functioning rotor-driving setup.
The atmospheric system produces distinct leaves and dust with the complete requested gravity, Wind, and Turbulence behavior.
The complete final lighting system combines a genuine dusk HDRI with exactly one contributing Sun lamp and visibly produces dusk illumination.
The selected storyboard render coherently presents the open-field turbine from the requested camera with effective depth of field and motion blur.
The requested final render and retained editable .blend form one valid Cycles-configured project outcome.

notes: This is a recognizable wind-turbine dusk storyboard with sound overall placement, scale cues, and camera mood. Its principal weaknesses are the simplified/unverifiable internal nacelle systems, the visibly artificial floating confetti and particle cloud, minimal material differentiation, and lack of visual evidence for the requested spinning, motion blur, and force-driven animation.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
